title: Hierarchy within the New York local
summary: Studio, symphony, Broadway, club date strata.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Because our musicians' membership, in a way it's our own fault because we are so divided. Take the New York local, it's stratified. Going back a few years when there was a lot of -- at the very peak was the so-called outside musicians, the studio musician. Now, sort of at the peak over to the side was the symphony musicians and the opera musicians, but only in terms of respect, not in terms of economy, because they almost starved to death. They made terrible salaries in those days.

And then right under that would be the commercial musicians. Then the stage below that would be the Broadway show musicians. Then the bands, the steady bands in the clubs, then the club date musicians. And quite often the club date musicians were probably making more than anybody because some of those slick ones could make an awful lot of money. But

just in the hierarchy -- now, each one of these factions hoped that the faction above or all factions above or whatever -- this is not my ____________ categorizing, I mean, this is just the way people looked at it, including the guys who were, so-called, down below, looked up and hoped that the guys above would fall on their butts because maybe they'd have a chance.
